newsitem.title: USA: Gore announces first-time pact by U.S. communities.
newsitem.headline: Gore announces first-time pact by U.S. communities.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore said on Wednesday that U.S. cities and counties have formed an unprecedented pact to improve local job creation, environmental protection and social services.
Gore and municipal leaders announced the nation's Joint Center for Sustainable Communities in a press statement issued by the National Association of Counties and U.S. Conference of Mayors.
"It represents the first time a formal alliance has been forged between cities and counties at a national level," the groups said.
The new center will help localities carry out recommendations made in January 1996 by the President Clinton's Council on Sustainable Development, the groups said.

Michael Hightower, president of the National Association of Counties, said the alliance will help support "demonstration projects" that tackle key community issues like "brownfields" and how to better manage local governments.
"Brownfields" are local sites that have been lightly contaminated by previous industrial use, but fail to qualify as Superfund sites.
